simple.meaning: מַנְדַּע (mandaʻ) is a Hebrew concept word meaning “wisdom or intelligence.” BibleIQ follows how Scripture develops this idea across its occurrences.
simple.biblicalBackground: The concept appears 4 times across Daniel, beginning at Daniel 2:21. Its contexts include family line, Torah, kingship.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to מַנְדַּע (H4486).
simple.whyItMatters: Concept words shape biblical themes. BibleIQ keeps the concept grounded in actual verse evidence instead of starting with a later theological definition.
simple.summary: מַנְדַּע (mandaʻ) / H4486 is traced through Daniel 2:21, Daniel 4:31, Daniel 4:33, Daniel 5:12 as a generated source-based concept entry.

firstOccurrence.englishText: He changes the times and the seasons.

timeline.evidenceText: He changes the times and the seasons.
While the word was in the king’s mouth, a voice came from the sky, saying, “O king Nebuchadnezzar, to you it is spoken: ‘The kingdom has departed from you.

This was fulfilled the same hour on Nebuchadnezzar. He was driven from men, and ate grass as oxen, and his body was wet with the dew of the sky, until his hair had grown like eagles’ feathers, and his nails like birds’ claws.

because an excellent spirit, knowledge, understanding, interpreting of dreams, showing of dark sentences, and dissolving of doubts were found in the same Daniel, whom the king named Belteshazzar. Now let Daniel be called, and he will show the interpretation.”
